column4: Visit note | 2026-08-22 11:30 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Ashraf Kabir, 80, male. Mr. Kabir reports experiencing dizziness whenever he looks up, along with nausea accompanying the spinning sensation. He mentions that the issue began after a viral cold in Lalbagh. He works as a madrasa teacher and denies any recent falls, hearing loss, or weakness. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the right side, BP 134/74 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 57 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and coordination is normal. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2026-08-25 03:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Nargis Akand, 62, female. Mrs. Akand describes experiencing brief spinning when turning in bed, accompanied by nausea with the spinning. She states it started after a long bus ride to Chattogram. She is a software developer and has a history of Hypothyroidism, for which she takes regular medication. She denies any tinnitus, double vision, or fainting spells. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the right side, BP 113/80 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 72 kg. Reflexes are normal and there is no spontaneous nystagmus. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
